statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Oracle's verified earnings beat improves AI sentiment, while oil above $107 and Treasury yields near 4.95% keep macro stress extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the blocking threshold because a persistent one-way NQ path with shallow or failed retracements is not independently verified.
headline: Oracle beat offsets some technology pressure; oil and yields keep Stress extreme
body: Oracle reported first-quarter revenue of $19.3 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.92, with shares up about 7% after hours. The Nasdaq Composite closed 0.65% lower, the 10-year Treasury yield was near 4.95%, and Brent settled at $107.63. Cross-asset stress is extreme, but current exact NQ path evidence is insufficient to establish persistent mean-reversion failure.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours, Tail ranged from 18 to 34. It moved from low/WATCH overnight to elevated after PPI, peaked at 34, and returned to WATCH as the cash-session decline remained retracing rather than persistently one-way. Stress stayed near or at extreme.
outlookSummary: Oracle's after-hours beat is the immediate technology checkpoint, while the oil and yield shock keeps Stress extreme. Overnight Tail can ease if futures remain two-way. Friday CPI at 12:30 UTC is the next major risk window; later Tail escalation is conditional on realized directional persistence and failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: The Oracle call and immediate after-hours digestion remain the active checkpoint. Tail stays at WATCH unless a sustained index-level move develops with shallow or failed retracements.
As the Oracle impulse ages, two-way futures trade would allow a slight Tail easing. A broad AI-led extension that holds extremes would invalidate that easing.
Early overnight conditions favor modest Tail normalization if price discovery rotates rather than trends. Oil above $100 keeps Stress near extreme despite that path assumption.
During the Asia handoff, meaningful retracements and lower directional efficiency would keep Tail contained. A clean breakout with shallow pullbacks would be adverse.
Early Asia remains conditionally lower-Tail if volatility compresses and neither side holds session extremes. Repeated extension after failed pullbacks would reverse the easing.
Without a scheduled U.S. catalyst in this hour, rotational trade would keep Tail near the low end of WATCH. Alignment of rates, oil and a directional NQ move would raise concern.
Thin overnight liquidity keeps path quality central. Continued mean-reverting swings would preserve the lower Tail estimate; persistent extreme-holding would not.
Late-Asia extensions that are absorbed would keep Tail contained. Failure to retrace repeated pushes would be the main condition for a higher regime assessment.
Approaching Europe, cross-asset reopening can reintroduce volatility. Tail remains WATCH if futures continue to retrace materially rather than establish directional efficiency.
European trading can test whether the oil-and-yield shock is still transmitting into technology risk. Two-way NQ structure would keep Tail contained.
As U.S. participation builds, oil, Treasury yields and semiconductor behavior become more informative. Tail stays below block levels unless directional alignment strengthens.
Premarket liquidity should improve evidence quality. A balanced response to overnight catalysts supports WATCH; persistent one-way repricing would raise Tail.
CPI approaches within two hours. The event itself raises Stress and evidence sensitivity more than Tail; pre-release Tail remains WATCH absent an already persistent directional path.
The final pre-CPI hour carries extreme Stress. Tail remains at the WATCH ceiling unless live price structure is already showing repeated extension or failed retracements.
CPI is scheduled for 12:30 UTC. The first reaction should be judged on realized retracement quality; the release alone does not establish a pathological one-way path.

In the first full post-CPI hour, Tail is conditionally elevated because existing oil and yield stress could amplify a directional repricing. Meaningful retracements would pull the assessment back toward WATCH.
The U.S. cash-open transition and preliminary Michigan sentiment create a second path checkpoint. Sustained extension through the open would keep Tail elevated; two-way rotation would reduce it.
After the opening impulse, persistent extreme-holding would sustain elevated Tail. A broad retracement across technology and semiconductors would argue for faster normalization.
Mid-session Tail remains modestly elevated only if the CPI/opening sequence continues to resist mean reversion. Stabilizing yields and repeated pullbacks would lower it.
If the event impulse has become two-way by late afternoon, Tail returns to WATCH while Stress remains high from oil, rates and inflation uncertainty.
Late-session conditions favor further Tail easing if NQ no longer holds an extreme and cross-assets stop reinforcing one direction.
Into the closing phase, orderly rotation would keep Tail below the block threshold. A renewed one-way push would be the main adverse deviation from this path.
After the cash close, the forecast assumes the CPI-driven impulse has largely been digested. Tail stays near low-WATCH levels unless after-hours structure reaccelerates directionally.

forecastDetail.comment: Oracle's verified beat is positive for AI sentiment, while oil and yields remain severe stressors; live NQ one-way structure is not verified.
The Oracle call remains the immediate checkpoint; WATCH persists unless after-hours index structure becomes persistently directional.
Two-way digestion of the earnings impulse supports slight Tail easing; sustained AI-led extension would negate it.
Overnight rotation supports lower Tail, while the oil shock keeps Stress near extreme.
At the Asia handoff, retracement depth is the key path test; shallow pullbacks would be adverse.
Early Asia is conditionally lower-Tail if volatility compresses and extremes are not held.
